strengths: A distinctive lantern-lit canal city, with authored district landmarks, portraits, goods and writing.
A readable persistent HUD, per-good sparklines, average cargo cost, explicit sale profit and dated remote quotes.
A genuinely spatial map with animated journeys, current location, waypoints, danger, fleet calls and held-cargo opportunities.
Complete touch settlement and clean regressions, including offline file access, restricted storage and committed event reloads.
weaknesses: Dense phone sheets put price history and complete remote comparisons below the fold.
Small route cards truncate quote warnings; comparing several held goods needs another sheet.
The five-step tour explains the loop rather than teaching through a first transaction.
Some desktop controls are compact; no physical-device or audible-quality validation was possible.

bugs.what: The normal-speed first-buy help toast visually covers the market heading, wireless calendar button and route recommendation. It does not intercept taps.
bugs.repro: Fresh run at 390×844, finish the tour, open Glowkelp, type 10, confirm Buy, and inspect about 1.2 seconds later. The firstbuy hint appears 400ms after purchase and lasts 4500ms. See explore-bought.png; source hint() and #toasts place it immediately below the HUD.

evidence.phone_notes: One complete actual-UI automated touch/typing game in WebKit at 390×844, seed 97: day 30, all seven ports, 29 voyages, 791 recorded actions, ¤486,796 Tide Baron, ¤0 debt, 70 capacity, 100% hull, persistent ledger. This is UI automation, not a claimed human full run. I independently directed a separate normal-speed WebKit exploration through nights 1–4: all tour steps, buy/sell, quantity edges, port details, two-night waypoint, event decisions, bank deposit/withdrawal, HUD explanation and staying overnight. I checked 390×664, 360×640 and 430×932 as well as 390×844, and personally inspected representative screenshots. The full automated touch run and verification UI use FAST=true and reduced motion; my independent harness exploration did not enable FAST.
evidence.desktop_notes: Frozen verification used actual Chromium desktop mouse/keyboard at 1280×800. My separate normal-speed Chromium 1280×800 harness used touch/mobile emulation plus real key presses, so I do not mislabel that exploration as a physical desktop mouse session. I inspected both desktop layouts, selected a port with 6, sailed with Enter, exercised M mute/resume and took the gull risk. Two complete Chromium game-function regressions ended at ¤81,678 and ¤619,375. Those are function-driven runs, not touch play.
evidence.audio_notes: Windows WebKit lacks Web Audio. Its labelled gesture-policy stand-in can check unlock/scheduling only. My real Chromium context was running, became suspended after M, and resumed during keydown after M again. I inspected the synthesized sound and ambience definitions. I did not hear or assess audible quality, physical-iPhone output, silent-switch behavior or audio latency.
method_boundaries: The scored full touch game used only local/public observations and real taps/typed inputs. Only initial deterministic seeding and documented animation acceleration were applied; no hidden outcomes were read or resources mutated.
Event and late-night UI/storage/sandbox tests are explicit fixtures, separate from ordinary scored gameplay.

The optional four-policy comparison is function-driven and uses the frozen adapter's per-night event reseeding for paired comparisons. Its 64 games and round-trip probes are controlled supplementary evidence, not ordinary UI play or an unbiased human sample.
The profile uses one normal-speed function-driven Chromium voyage and 40 fixture restarts. Its frame/heap numbers do not establish physical-iPhone or full-run performance.
No physical phone, browser toolbar/safe-area changes, software keyboard, screen reader, audible quality or complete normal-speed human game was covered.
execution_model_issues: Model matched the requested gpt-6.1-sol. No delegation, git writes, game edits or helper edits.
The documented Node PATH prefix was used; all supplied suites completed successfully.

One exploratory selector incorrectly assumed the eel's Walk on key was leave. No matching element was found; I used the visible Walk on text and continued. This was a driver selection error, not a game error.
One image lookup omitted the fixture's -offer suffix; I corrected the path and inspected the actual offer/outcome screenshots.
evidence.weighted_calculation: sum(score * frozen criterion weight / 10); weights total 100
evidence.browser_cleanup: Both independent harnesses (9472 and 9482) were stopped successfully before final handback; all supplied suites completed and closed their browsers.

verdict: A cohesive, expressive and highly playable trading game. The illustrated canal map and financial feedback are its strongest surfaces. Phone information density, temporary toast overlap and limited shortcut discoverability keep the interaction design below the top anchor. No score cap was triggered.
